title: 3rd Stopping Place 2nd Truth From The Comprehensiveness Of Mercifulness To Unity And Oneness

questions.question: In the opening comparison, what natural example is used to help explain unity and oneness?
questions.answer: The example is the sun, its light, and its reflection in bright and clear things.

questions.question: What feature of sunlight points to unity in the comparison?
questions.answer: Its light reaches and includes everything that faces it.

questions.question: What feature of sunlight points to oneness in the comparison?
questions.answer: Its reflection appears closely in many separate objects at the same time.

questions.question: When someone sees sunlight spread everywhere, what conclusion should that person reach?
questions.answer: He should understand that the sun is one and unique.

questions.question: What does seeing the sun’s reflection in shining objects and water drops suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests that the sun’s effects are present near many things at once.

questions.question: In the passage, what does the all-embracing mercy of Allah show?
questions.answer: It shows His unity and that He has no partner.

questions.question: Besides mercy itself, what is said to be found in everything, especially in living beings and most of all in human beings?
questions.answer: Signs of many Divine Names and a kind of manifestation connected to His essence are found there.

questions.question: What does life give to an individual according to the passage?
questions.answer: It gives a broad capacity that connects the person to the whole universe.

questions.question: How does that broad capacity support the idea of oneness?
questions.answer: It shows that the One who gives life is present with all things and acts in all things.

questions.question: Through what does the Merciful One display the majesty of His glory across the universe and the earth?
questions.answer: He displays it through the unity and wide reach of His mercy.

questions.question: What happens in every member of living species through the manifestation of oneness?
questions.answer: Samples of all kinds of Divine gifts are gathered together in each one.

questions.question: What special point is made about human beings in this part of the passage?
questions.answer: Human beings receive a concentrated display of many different Divine favors.

questions.question: What everyday object is used to explain how man relates to the wider cosmos?
questions.answer: A melon and its seed are used as the example.

questions.question: Why must the maker of the seed also be the maker of the melon?
questions.answer: Because the seed is drawn from the melon, gathered in a measured way, and given its form by the same knowing and wise maker.

questions.question: What does the passage say would be impossible regarding the seed?
questions.answer: It would be impossible for anyone other than the one maker of the melon to make the seed.

questions.question: In the final comparison, what does the cosmos become like, what does the earth become like, and what does man become like?
questions.answer: The cosmos becomes like a tree or garden, the earth like a fruit or melon, and man like a seed.

questions.question: What final conclusion is drawn from that comparison?
questions.answer: The One who creates and sustains even the smallest living being must also be the Creator of the whole earth and the whole cosmos.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the comparison with the sun?
questions.answer: It is used to explain how unity and oneness can be understood through a familiar example.

questions.question: How does the sun’s light relate to everything turned toward it?
questions.answer: It surrounds and reaches all of them.

questions.question: What appears in every clear and polished object that receives sunlight?
questions.answer: A reflection of the sun’s light, warmth, and colors appears there.

questions.question: Why does widespread sunlight lead a person to recognize one sun rather than many?
questions.answer: Because one shared light covering many things points back to a single source.

questions.question: Why do reflections in many small objects support the idea of oneness?
questions.answer: Because they show the same source appearing near countless separate things without being divided.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does Divine mercy do in a way similar to sunlight?
questions.answer: It encompasses all things and reaches them broadly.

questions.question: What doctrinal point is proven by mercy’s reach over all things?
questions.answer: It proves Allah’s unity and denies any partner beside Him.

questions.question: Where are the signs of many Divine Names said to be especially visible?
questions.answer: They are especially visible in all living beings, and even more in human beings.

questions.question: What effect does life have on a person’s relation to the universe?
questions.answer: It gives the person a wide-ranging connection with the universe as a whole.

questions.question: What does that universal relation show about Allah’s action?
questions.answer: It shows that He is near all things and carries out His works within all things.

questions.question: How is Divine glory shown throughout the cosmos in this passage?
questions.answer: It is shown through mercy that is both unified and comprehensive.

questions.question: What is gathered together in each living creature?
questions.answer: Samples of many Divine bounties are gathered together in each one.

questions.question: How are the equipment and capacities of living things described?
questions.answer: They are arranged in an ordered way as part of Divine care.

questions.question: What does the passage say about Allah’s attention to each individual?
questions.answer: It says each individual receives special care and favor.

questions.question: Why is man described as concentrated in relation to Divine bounty?
questions.answer: Because many forms of bounty are made known in a focused way within him.

questions.question: How does the melon-seed example reinforce the argument?
questions.answer: It shows that the one who produces the whole also produces the concentrated form taken from it.

questions.question: What larger conclusion follows from the image of cosmos, earth, and man as tree, fruit, and seed?
questions.answer: The Maker of even the smallest living thing must be the Maker of the entire created order.

questions.question: Which two theological ideas are illustrated by the example of the sun?
questions.answer: Unity and oneness.

questions.question: In the comparison, what does the sun’s general illumination represent?
questions.answer: It represents unity through one source reaching many things.

questions.question: In the comparison, what do the sun’s many reflections represent?
questions.answer: They represent oneness through the source’s nearness and presence in many places.

questions.question: What kinds of objects are able to display the sun’s reflection in this example?
questions.answer: Bright, clear, and reflective objects, including drops of water.

questions.question: What should a thoughtful observer understand from the sun shining over many things?
questions.answer: That the source of that light is single and unique.

questions.question: What should a thoughtful observer understand from the sun appearing in many reflections?
questions.answer: That the same source is manifest close to many things at once.

questions.question: What reality in creation is compared to the sun’s all-reaching light?
questions.answer: The all-encompassing mercy of Allah.

questions.question: What is the first conclusion drawn from that mercy?
questions.answer: That Allah is one and has no partner.

questions.question: What else appears under the covering of mercy, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Manifestations of many Divine Names and a sign related to His essence.

questions.question: Which created beings receive special emphasis in this discussion?
questions.answer: Living beings in general, and human beings in particular.

questions.question: What does life produce in the individual that is important for the argument?
questions.answer: It produces a comprehensiveness that links the individual to the whole universe.

questions.question: How does that comprehensiveness support belief in oneness?
questions.answer: It indicates that one Lord is acting everywhere and is near to all things.

questions.question: What does the Merciful One gather within each member of living species?
questions.answer: He gathers examples of all His favors within each one.

questions.question: What balance does the passage maintain between care for individuals and the order of the whole universe?
questions.answer: Each individual receives special care without any damage to the order of the whole.

questions.question: Why is man given a central place in this section?
questions.answer: Because many kinds of Divine favor are displayed in him in a concentrated way.

questions.question: What does the process involving the melon and its seed suggest about authorship in creation?
questions.answer: The producer of the part must also be the producer of the whole from which that part is taken.

questions.question: What final belief is the reader meant to reach from the seed analogy?
questions.answer: The Sustainer of the smallest living being is also the Sustainer of the earth and the cosmos.

questions.question: What image from nature begins this passage’s explanation of Divine realities?
questions.answer: The image of the sun shining and reflecting in many objects.

questions.question: What three aspects of the sun are mentioned as being reflected?
questions.answer: Its light, its warmth, and its colors.

questions.question: What does the broad spread of sunlight symbolize?
questions.answer: It symbolizes unity through a single reality reaching many things.

questions.question: What does the sun’s appearing in separate reflective objects symbolize?
questions.answer: It symbolizes oneness through intimate presence with many things.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the sun’s relation to reflective things?
questions.answer: It presents the sun’s effects as being very near them, almost at their center.

questions.question: What Divine attribute is compared to light in the next part of the passage?
questions.answer: Mercy.

questions.question: What is proven by mercy’s encompassing all things?
questions.answer: Allah’s unity and the impossibility of any partner sharing in His rule.

questions.question: What is said to exist in everything under the covering of mercy?
questions.answer: Traces of many Divine Names and a kind of manifestation connected to Him.

questions.question: In which beings is this especially noticeable?
questions.answer: In living beings, and most especially in human beings.

questions.question: What does life give a human being besides mere existence?
questions.answer: It gives a broad scope that relates him to the whole universe.

questions.question: What does a human being’s relation to the whole universe indicate about the Creator?
questions.answer: It indicates that the Creator is present with all things and works in all things.

questions.question: How is the glory of the Merciful One displayed in the cosmos?
questions.answer: It is displayed through mercy that is both united and far-reaching.

questions.question: What does Allah gather together in every living member of each species?
questions.answer: He gathers examples of His many gifts.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the arrangement of the organs and tools of living creatures?
questions.answer: They are set in order as part of a deliberate and caring design.

questions.question: What special treatment does each individual receive?
questions.answer: Each one receives particular care and attention.

questions.question: How is man described in relation to Divine gifts?
questions.answer: He is described as a concentrated summary of many kinds of bounty.

questions.question: What chain of comparison leads to the final conclusion of the passage?
questions.answer: The cosmos is like a tree or garden, the earth like a fruit, and man like a seed, so the Maker of the seed must be the Maker of the whole.

questions.question: What lesson does the passage draw from sunlight reaching all visible things?
questions.answer: One source can affect many things together, which points to unity.

questions.question: What lesson does it draw from sunlight being reflected in many separate objects?
questions.answer: The same source can be present in relation to many individuals, which points to oneness.

questions.question: Why are drops of water mentioned along with larger bright objects?
questions.answer: To show that even the smallest reflective thing can display signs of the same sun.

questions.question: What human response is expected after seeing the sun’s all-reaching light?
questions.answer: A person should recognize that there is one sun, not many suns.

questions.question: What human response is expected after seeing the sun’s reflection in many things?
questions.answer: A person should understand that the same sun is near those many things through its qualities.

questions.question: What in the created world functions like sunlight in the spiritual argument?
questions.answer: The all-encompassing mercy of Allah.

questions.question: What two beliefs are supported by that mercy?
questions.answer: That Allah is one, and that He has no partner.

questions.question: What is the significance of Divine Names being manifested in everything?
questions.answer: It shows that creation carries many signs of Allah’s attributes.

questions.question: Why are living beings given special attention in this argument?
questions.answer: Because those signs appear in them more clearly, especially in human beings.

questions.question: What does life do for the individual according to the passage?
questions.answer: It gives the individual a broad relation to the rest of existence.

questions.question: How does that relation strengthen the proof of oneness?
questions.answer: It points to one Lord who manages all levels of existence together.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by gathering samples of all bounties in each living member?
questions.answer: It means each living thing carries many kinds of Divine favor within itself.

questions.question: How can individuals receive special care without harming the whole order of the universe?
questions.answer: Because the same Merciful Lord manages both the whole and the parts perfectly.

questions.question: In what sense is man like a summary?
questions.answer: Many different blessings are shown together in him in a focused form.

questions.question: What does the melon-seed example teach about ownership and control in creation?
questions.answer: Whoever makes the complete thing is also the one who makes its concentrated form.

questions.question: Why is it impossible for another maker to produce the seed alone?
questions.answer: Because the seed is tied to the whole fruit by measured knowledge and wise arrangement.

questions.question: What conclusion does the passage draw about the Creator of the smallest living being?
questions.answer: That Creator must also be the Creator and Sustainer of the earth and the entire cosmos.

questions.question: What comparison does the passage use first to make an abstract idea easier to grasp?
questions.answer: It uses the example of the sun and its light.

questions.question: How does the sun’s light serve as a sign of unity?
questions.answer: It extends over all receptive things from one source.

questions.question: How do reflections of the sun serve as a sign of oneness?
questions.answer: They show the same source appearing in many individual places at once.

questions.question: What kinds of things are said to receive those reflections?
questions.answer: Shining and transparent things, even tiny water drops.

questions.question: What conclusion about the sun follows from seeing one light spread over many things?
questions.answer: The observer concludes that the sun is single and unique.

questions.question: What further conclusion follows from seeing reflected sunlight in many objects?
questions.answer: The observer sees that the same sun’s qualities are near all those objects.

questions.question: What Divine reality is said to surround all things in a similar way?
questions.answer: The mercy of the Merciful One.

questions.question: What does that surrounding mercy prove?
questions.answer: It proves Divine unity and rules out any partner.

questions.question: What lies beneath the covering of mercy in all things?
questions.answer: Manifestations of many Divine Names and a sign of Divine self-disclosure.

questions.question: Which beings most clearly show this reality?
questions.answer: Living beings, especially human beings.

questions.question: What special quality comes from life in the individual?
questions.answer: A wide-ranging capacity that makes the individual connected to the whole universe.

questions.question: What does this wide-ranging capacity reveal about Allah’s relation to creation?
questions.answer: It reveals that He is with all things and active in all things.

questions.question: How does the passage describe Allah’s treatment of each member of living species?
questions.answer: He gathers many examples of His gifts in each one and arranges their means and faculties.

questions.question: What does the passage say about Allah’s care for each individual?
questions.answer: It says each one receives special and beautiful care.

questions.question: Why is man compared to a seed?
questions.answer: Because he contains in concentrated form many meanings and gifts connected to the larger whole.

questions.question: How does the melon and seed analogy support the claim about the Creator?
questions.answer: It shows that only the maker of the whole fruit can make the seed drawn from it.

questions.question: State the final conclusion of the passage in one sentence.
questions.answer: The Lord who creates and sustains even the smallest living being is the same Lord who creates and sustains the whole earth and the whole cosmos.
